chunks: Al-Saffar, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Muhammad ibn Aslam al-Jabali, from al-Husayn ibn Khalid and others, from Abu al-Hasan al-Rida عليه السلام.

key_terms.أَبِي اَلْحَسَنِ اَلرِّضَا عَلَيْهِ اَلس: Imam al-Rida عليه السلام, the authority from whom the report is narrated
key_terms.اَلصَّفَّارُ: Al-Saffar, the first transmitter named in the sanad
key_terms.اَلْحُسَيْنِ بْنِ خَالِدٍ: Al-Husayn ibn Khalid, a narrator transmitting from the Imam
key_terms.مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ أَسْلَمَ اَلْجَبَلِيِّ: Muhammad ibn Aslam al-Jabali, a narrator in the chain
key_terms.مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ اَلْحُسَيْنِ: Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, a narrator in the chain
key_terms.مِثْلَهُ: Meaning: the same as the previous hadith text

ai.seo_question: What does the abbreviated hadith wording "مِثْلَهُ" mean in Tahdhib al-Ahkam?
ai.summary: This report contains an isnad ending with Imam al-Rida عليه السلام, but its matn is abbreviated with the word "mithlahu," indicating that it is the same as the preceding hadith. Its significance is therefore dependent on the immediately previous narration in the chapter, while this entry chiefly serves as a supporting transmission.
